newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina lifts trade deficit forecast to $2.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina lifts trade deficit forecast to $2.0 bln.

text.p: Argentina revised its 1997 trade deficit estimate to $2.0 billion from $1.5 billion, the Industry Secretariat said Wednesday night.
Total exports were estimated at $28 billion, up 16.7 percent from last year, while imports were seen growing 25 percent to $30 billion.
Imports of capital goods would reach 45 percent of all imports in 1997 against 40 percent in 1996, it said.

The Secretariat also released preliminary growth figures for different sectors, with car production expected to increase 29.3 percent in May compared with the same month last year and domestic sales of steel and cement seen rising 22.2 percent and 29.2 percent, respectively.
May year-on-year energy consumption growth was seen at 8.6 percent.
Imports of capital goods and manufactured goods were forecast to rise 49.5 percent and 16.7 percent year-on-year in April, respectively.
In the 1996-1997 period, consumption was seen providing only 50 percent of growth in aggregate demand, which would be the lowest since 1953.
But exports were seen providing 18 percent of growth in aggregate demand, the highest since 1953, and investment was seen accounting for 32 percent of the growth in aggregate demand.
Foreign direct investment in Argentina was estimated at $33.8 billion between 1997 and 2000, and at $8.0 billion this year, compared with $5.0 billion last year.
Chemicals and petrochemicals will account for the biggest growth in foreign investment in the four-year period, rising 19.1 percent.

Finally, oil exports were expected to be worth $4.0 billion annually by the year 2000 and natural gas exports to be worth between $500 million and $600 million. Mining exports were seen at $1.3 billion annually by the year 2000.
